input.task: Write the investment thesis and the recommendation on COSTCO WHOLESALE CORP /NEW (COST) from the two analysts' outputs.

overview.claim: Costco operates membership warehouses in the U.S., Puerto Rico, Canada, Mexico, Japan and other countries in Asia, Europe and Oceania.
overview.quote: We are principally engaged in the operation of membership warehouses in the United States (U.S.) and Puerto Rico, Canada, Mexico, Japan, the United Kingdom (U.K.), Korea, Australia, Taiwan, China, Spain, France, Sweden, Iceland, and New Zealand.

overview.claim: The company earns money by selling a limited selection of branded and private-label products at low prices, which aims to produce high sales volumes and rapid inventory turnover.
overview.quote: We operate membership warehouses and e-commerce sites based on the concept that offering low prices on a limited selection of nationally-branded and private-label products in a wide range of categories will produce high sales volumes and rapid inventory turnover.

overview.claim: Members pay an annual fee, which is $65 in the U.S. and includes a free household card.
overview.quote: Our annual fee for memberships is $65 in the U.S., varies in other countries and includes a free household card.

business_model.claim: Costco reports three operating segments, U.S., Canadian and Other International, which use generally the same operating model.
business_model.quote: Our operating models are generally the same across our U.S., Canadian, and Other International operating segments (see Note 11 to the consolidated financial statements included in Item 8 of this Report).

business_model.claim: Its customers are paid members, who numbered 84,100 thousand at the latest year end, up from 81,000 thousand and 76,200 thousand in the two prior years.
Membership fees are a separate revenue source, totaling $5,907 million in the latest fiscal year, up from $5,323 million the year before.
Gasoline made up 11% of total net sales in 2026.
business_model.quote: Our gasoline business represented 11% of total net sales in 2026.

competitive_position.claim: Costco operated 939 warehouses worldwide at August 30, 2026, up from 914 a year earlier.
competitive_position.quote: Costco operated 939, 914, and 890 warehouses worldwide at August 30, 2026, August 31, 2025, and September 1, 2024.

competitive_position.claim: The member renewal rate was 92.3% in the U.S. and Canada and 89.8% worldwide at the end of 2026.
competitive_position.quote: Our member renewal rate was 92.3% in the U.S. and Canada and 89.8% worldwide at the end of 2026.

competitive_position.claim: The filing names Walmart, Target, Kroger and Amazon as significant general merchandise competitors in the U.S.
competitive_position.quote: Walmart, Target, Kroger, and Amazon are among our significant general merchandise retail competitors in the U.S.

competitive_position.claim: Management says higher tariffs are more likely to hurt results than to help them.
competitive_position.quote: Higher tariffs are more likely to adversely impact rather than improve our results.

catalysts.claim: Management names growth in net sales, particularly comparable sales, as the most important driver of profitability.
catalysts.quote: We believe that the most important driver of our profitability is increasing net sales, particularly comparable sales.

catalysts.claim: Costco plans to open up to 33 new warehouses, including five relocations, in 2027.
catalysts.quote: We opened 28 new warehouses, including three relocations, in 2026, and plan to open up to 33 new warehouses, including five relocations, in 2027.

catalysts.claim: Management intends to spend approximately $7,500 million on capital expenditures in fiscal 2027, up from $6,435 million in 2026.
catalysts.quote: In 2026, we spent $6,435 on capital expenditures, and it is our current intention to spend approximately $7,500 during fiscal 2027.

catalysts.claim: The company expects to keep increasing the sales penetration of its private-label items.
catalysts.quote: We expect to continue to increase the sales penetration of our private-label items.

recent_developments.claim: Net sales for the fiscal year rose 10.1 percent to $297.2 billion from $269.9 billion.
recent_developments.quote: Net sales for the fiscal year increased 10.1 percent, to $297.2 billion, from $269.9 billion last year.

recent_developments.claim: Net income for the fiscal year rose to $9.226 billion, or $20.76 per diluted share, from $8.099 billion, or $18.21 per diluted share.
recent_developments.quote: Net income for the fiscal year was $9.226 billion, $20.76 per diluted share, compared to $8.099 billion, $18.21 per diluted share, last year.

recent_developments.claim: Fourth-quarter results included a non-recurring benefit of $0.15 per diluted share from IEEPA tariff refunds, less partial reinvestment of those refunds in member values.
recent_developments.quote: This year's fourth quarter was positively impacted by a non-recurring benefit of $0.15 per diluted share from IEEPA tariff refunds received in the quarter, less partial reinvestment of those refunds in increased member values.

recent_developments.claim: In April 2026 the Board raised the quarterly cash dividend from $1.30 to $1.47 per share.
recent_developments.quote: In April 2026, the Board of Directors increased our quarterly cash dividend from $1.30 to $1.47 per share.

financial_analyst.statement_analysis:
### Costco Wholesale (COST): fiscal year ended 2026-08-30 (FY2026) against fiscal year ended 2025-08-31 (FY2025)
All figures are in $ millions except per-share data. Each comes from 10-K 0000909832-26-000093, filed 2026-10-07. FY2026 covers 2025-09-01 to 2026-08-30. FY2025 covers 2024-09-02 to 2025-08-31.

**Growth**
- **Total revenue:** $303,154.0M against $275,235.0M (us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax). Growth is **10.14%** = 303,154.0 / 275,235.0 - 1.
- **Operating income:** $11,685.0M against $10,383.0M (us-gaap:OperatingIncomeLoss). Growth is **12.54%** = 11,685.0 / 10,383.0 - 1.
- **Net income attributable to Costco:** $9,226.0M against $8,099.0M (us-gaap:NetIncomeLoss). Growth is **13.92%** = 9,226.0 / 8,099.0 - 1.
- **GAAP diluted EPS:** $20.76 against $18.21 (us-gaap:EarningsPerShareDiluted). Growth is **14.00%** = 20.76 / 18.21 - 1.
- Profits grew faster than revenue at each level: operating income grew 12.54%, net income 13.92% and EPS 14.00%, against revenue growth of 10.14%.

**Margins**
- **Operating margin:** **3.85%** in FY2026 (= 11,685.0 / 303,154.0) against **3.77%** in FY2025 (= 10,383.0 / 275,235.0).
- **Net margin:** **3.04%** in FY2026 (= 9,226.0 / 303,154.0) against **2.94%** in FY2025 (= 8,099.0 / 275,235.0).
- Margins are thin, as expected for a warehouse-club model, and both widened modestly year on year.

**Returns on equity**
- **Stockholders' equity** (us-gaap:StockholdersEquity) was $35,803.0M at 2026-08-30 and $29,164.0M at 2025-08-31.
- **Return on average equity:** **28.40%** = 9,226.0 / ((35,803.0 + 29,164.0) / 2).
- ROE on year-end equity is not in the context. It is requested in calculator_requests.

**Leverage**
- **Debt components** at 2026-08-30 against 2025-08-31:
  - Long-term debt excluding current maturities (us-gaap:LongTermDebtNoncurrent): $3,914.0M against $5,713.0M.
  - Current portion (us-gaap:LongTermDebtCurrent): $2,248.0M against $75.0M.
- **Debt to equity:** **0.172** at FY2026 year end (= (3,914.0 + 2,248.0) / 35,803.0) against **0.198** at FY2025 year end (= (5,713.0 + 75.0) / 29,164.0).
- The current portion rose sharply, from $75.0M to $2,248.0M, because debt moved into the within-one-year maturity bucket. The long-term portion fell. Total debt in dollars is requested in calculator_requests.
- Leverage is low. The ratio fell because equity grew faster than debt.
- The debt figures exclude lease liabilities, which are not in the context.

**Cash flow**
- **Cash from operations** (us-gaap:NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities): $15,817.0M against $13,335.0M. Growth is **18.61%** = 15,817.0 / 13,335.0 - 1.
- **Additions to property and equipment** (us-gaap:PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment): $6,435.0M against $5,498.0M. Growth is **17.04%** = 6,435.0 / 5,498.0 - 1.
- **Free cash flow:**
  - FY2026: **$9,382.0M** = 15,817.0 - 6,435.0.
  - FY2025: **$7,837.0M** = 13,335.0 - 5,498.0.
  - Growth: **19.71%** = (15,817.0 - 6,435.0) / (13,335.0 - 5,498.0) - 1.
- **Free cash flow margin:** **3.09%** = (15,817.0 - 6,435.0) / 303,154.0.
- **Free cash flow / net income:** **1.02** = (15,817.0 - 6,435.0) / 9,226.0. Earnings are fully backed by free cash flow, even with capital spending rising 17.04%.
financial_analyst.latest_quarter:
### Q4 FY2026: 16 weeks ended August 30, 2026, against 16 weeks ended August 31, 2025

**Source**
- 8-K accession 0000909832-26-000084, Item 2.02, Exhibit 99.1, accepted 2026-09-24 16:17:37 ET.
- Units, as stated in the release: "(dollars in millions, except per share data) (unaudited)".

**Revenue**
- Release lines:
  - "Net sales | $93,873 | $84,432 | $297,247 | $269,912"
  - "Membership fees | 1,850 | 1,724 | 5,907 | 5,323"
  - "Total revenue | 95,723 | 86,156 | 303,154 | 275,235"
- Quarter total revenue was **$95,723M** against **$86,156M**.
- Growth on the same quarter last year was **11.10%** = 95,723 / 86,156 - 1, using the first two columns of the total revenue line.
- The 52-week columns (303,154 and 275,235) match the 10-K total revenue facts.

**GAAP diluted EPS**
- Release line, under "NET INCOME PER COMMON SHARE:": "Diluted | $6.75 | $5.87 | $20.76 | $18.21".
- Quarter GAAP diluted EPS was **$6.75** against **$5.87**.
- Growth was **14.99%** = 6.75 / 5.87 - 1, using the release's first two columns.

**Release commentary**
- "Net income for the fourth quarter was $2.998 billion, $6.75 per diluted share, compared to $2.610 billion, $5.87 per diluted share, last year."
- "This year's fourth quarter was positively impacted by a non-recurring benefit of $0.15 per diluted share from IEEPA tariff refunds received in the quarter, less partial reinvestment of those refunds in increased member values."
- The 14.99% quarterly EPS growth therefore includes this one-off benefit.
- EPS and growth excluding the $0.15 benefit are not in the context. Both are requested in calculator_requests and are not computed here.

| Walmart (WMT) | 2026-01-31 (FY ended Jan 2026) | 713,163.0 (us-gaap:Revenues) | 29,825.0 (us-gaap:OperatingIncomeLoss) | 4.18% = 29,825.0 / 713,163.0 | 10-K 0000104169-26-000055 |
| Target (TGT) | 2026-01-31 (FY ended Jan 2026) | 104,780.0 (us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax) | 5,117.0 (us-gaap:OperatingIncomeLoss) | 4.88% = 5,117.0 / 104,780.0 | 10-K 0000027419-26-000016 |
| BJ's Wholesale (BJ) | 2026-01-31 (FY ended Jan 2026) | 21,457.3 (us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax) | 816.6 (us-gaap:OperatingIncomeLoss) | 3.81% = 816.6 / 21,457.3 | 10-K 0001531152-26-000007 |

**Notes on comparability**
- Every margin uses the same definition: total revenue, including membership and other income, and GAAP operating income.
- Walmart's total revenue is tagged us-gaap:Revenues. The other three use RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax.
- The fiscal years differ. COST's year ends 2026-08-30, while the three peers' years end 2026-01-31. The periods overlap by only about five months.

**What the table shows**
- COST's 3.85% operating margin is:
  - below Target (4.88%) and Walmart (4.18%);
  - close to its closest club peer, BJ's (3.81%).
- On revenue, COST is the second largest of the four, behind Walmart.
- No peer prices or EPS are in the context, so a peer P/E comparison is not possible.
financial_analyst.valuation:
### Valuation

**P/E**
- **P/E = 47.8** = 992.13 / 20.76.
- Price: $992.13, given with --price. The context gives no date for this price.
- EPS: FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS of $20.76 (us-gaap:EarningsPerShareDiluted, 2025-09-01 to 2026-08-30, 10-K 0000909832-26-000093).
- P/E on FY2025 EPS of $18.21 is requested in calculator_requests.

**What the ratios say about value**
- At 47.8x trailing GAAP EPS, the market is paying a large premium for earnings growth of 14.00% (EPS) and 13.92% (net income).
- Business quality is high:
  - ROE on average equity is 28.40%.
  - Free cash flow covers net income 1.02 times.
  - Debt to equity is low, at 0.172.
- Margins are thin and only slowly widening: operating margin 3.85% against 3.77%, and net margin 3.04% against 2.94%.
- The latest quarter's EPS growth of 14.99% includes a non-recurring $0.15 tariff-refund benefit. Trailing EPS of $20.76 therefore contains that one-off item.
- No peer P/E is available in the context, so relative valuation cannot be assessed.
- No recommendation is given.
definitions: Revenue means total revenue (net sales plus membership fees), tagged us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax: $303,154.0M for FY2026. It is not net sales alone, which the release shows as $297,247M.
EPS means GAAP diluted EPS (us-gaap:EarningsPerShareDiluted); no adjusted EPS is used. The release's $0.15 non-recurring tariff-refund benefit is noted but not removed.
Return on equity uses average equity: net income divided by the mean of year-end FY2026 and FY2025 stockholders' equity attributable to Costco. ROE on year-end equity is requested separately.
Net income means net income attributable to Costco (us-gaap:NetIncomeLoss).
Debt means long-term debt excluding current maturities plus the current portion of long-term debt. Lease liabilities are excluded.
Free cash flow means net cash provided by operating activities minus payments to acquire property, plant and equipment.
Peer operating margins use total revenue and GAAP operating income for each company. Each figure is labelled with its own fiscal year end: 2026-08-30 for COST and 2026-01-31 for WMT, TGT and BJ.
Quarterly growth compares the 16 weeks ended August 30, 2026 with the 16 weeks ended August 31, 2025, as given in the release's first two columns.

deciding_number.label: what the number is
deciding_number.source: its source, as the Financial Analyst gave it

expected_output.strategic_recommendations: a list of 2 to 3 sentences for the client: what to watch or do next, each tied to a number or a quote in the context

deciding_number.label: P/E on FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS
deciding_number.source: Financial Analyst valuation: P/E = 47.8 = 992.13 / 20.76. The price of $992.13 was given with --price and the context gives no date for it. EPS is FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS of $20.76 (us-gaap:EarningsPerShareDiluted, 2025-09-01 to 2026-08-30, 10-K 0000909832-26-000093).

output.thesis: Costco is a high-quality compounder. FY2026 total revenue grew **10.14%** to $303,154.0M, and GAAP diluted EPS grew **14.00%** to $20.76. Return on average equity was **28.40%**, free cash flow was **$9,382.0M** (1.02 times net income) and debt to equity was a low **0.172**. The membership flywheel is intact: paid members rose to 84,100 thousand from 81,000 thousand, and the renewal rate was 92.3% in the U.S. and Canada and 89.8% worldwide. However, the shares trade at **47.8x** trailing GAAP EPS, a large premium for earnings growth of 14.00%. That EPS of $20.76 also includes a non-recurring $0.15 per diluted share tariff-refund benefit. With an operating margin of only 3.85% (against 3.77%), and no peer P/E in the context to show the premium is justified, the valuation already prices in the quality, so we rate it Hold rather than Buy.
output.what_would_change_it: We would move to Buy if the price fell enough to bring the P/E materially below 47.8 while EPS growth held at or above 14.00%. We would move to Sell if comparable-sales growth slowed or the renewal rate fell below 89.8% worldwide, since that would undercut the growth the 47.8x multiple assumes.
strategic_recommendations: Track comparable sales closely, because management calls increasing net sales, "particularly comparable sales," the most important driver of profitability, and that growth is what has to justify the 47.8x multiple.

Check that the planned approximately $7,500 of fiscal 2027 capital expenditures (in millions, against $6,435 in 2026) and the plan to open up to 33 new warehouses keep free cash flow at or above 1.02 times net income.

Watch for tariff effects. FY2026 EPS of $20.76 includes a non-recurring $0.15 per diluted share refund benefit, and management states that "higher tariffs are more likely to adversely impact rather than improve our results."
